collection_summary:
Original `top_k` instance that **SATURATES top_k at 5/5 — SIXTH CATEGORY TO FULLY CLEAR** (joining factual_lookup 6/5, multi_attribute_projection 8/8, set_operation 8/8, set_filter 5/5, causal 5/5). **Transportation/Aviation NEW subdomain** — the Transportation family extends from 2 instances (Road Traffic via `countries_that_drive_on_the_left`, Logistics via `worlds_largest_container_ports_by_2024_teu`) to 3 instances with this Ready, becoming a 3-subdomain family. Natural human query: 'What are the world's busiest airports — how many passengers does each handle annually, what country and city is each in, and what world region?'

Multi-wiki source plan (21 URLs): 1 Wikipedia 'List of busiest airports by passenger traffic' master article supplies the universe + ranking + Passengers value (the master article's '2025 statistics' section is sourced from Airports Council International / ACI); 20 per-airport Wikipedia articles supply per-row Country + City via infobox/lead. Region is a curator-assigned closed-vocabulary categorical (same 9-value vocab as the worlds_largest_container_ports_by_2024_teu instance).

Result: 20 rows × 5 columns (Airport PK + Country categorical + City categorical + Passengers (millions) numeric + Region categorical), single-key PK on Airport, 0 duplicates. Country distribution: United States 5 (dominates global airport rankings — Atlanta, DFW, O'Hare, Denver, LAX), China 4 (Shanghai Pudong, Guangzhou Baiyun, Beijing Capital, Shenzhen Bao'an), plus singletons for UAE, Japan, UK, Turkey, India, South Korea, France, Singapore, Netherlands, Spain, Malaysia (13 distinct countries). Region distribution: East Asia 6, North America 5, Europe 5 (including Istanbul per master grouping), Southeast Asia 2, South Asia 1, Middle East 1 (6 of 9 declared regions). Passenger range: 63.3 M (Kuala Lumpur) to 106.3 M (Atlanta) — 43 M span across the top-20.

Universe rule: top-20 airports by 2025 annual passenger traffic per Wikipedia 'List of busiest airports by passenger traffic' master article's '2025 statistics' section (ACI sourced). All 20 are operational as of source-access date 2026-05-14 (no construction-status exclusions; the master article does not maintain an under-construction split for airports — all ranked entries are active operational airports). Master ranking is the universe authority; per-airport articles supply non-time-series attribute values only.

Entity class: `engineered-structures/airports` (NEW fine-class in the `engineered-structures` bucket — bucket extends from 3 to 4 instances after this Ready, joining bridges + buildings + dams + airports).

**Canonical-source rule for time-series passenger-traffic metric** (same as ports — master-wins inversion of the bridges/dams per-entity-wins rule for static structural metrics): the master article wins for Passengers (millions) because ACI updates the master annually while per-airport Wikipedia article infoboxes lag (some are stale by 2+ years). For non-time-series attributes (Country, City), per-airport article wins (entity-detail role). For Region, curator-assigned closed-vocab per the documented country-to-region mapping. This rule is established by the cycle-1 ports instance and applied uniformly here; future time-series-throughput top-K instances should cite both ports + airports as the canonical precedent.
source_coverage_notes:
Twenty-one Wikipedia source URLs combine. One 'List of busiest airports by passenger traffic' master article defines the universe + ranking + 2025 Passengers values (ACI sourced); 20 per-airport articles supply per-row Country + City via infobox/lead. Region is a curator-assigned closed-vocabulary categorical from a 9-value vocab not directly sourced from per-airport articles.

Roles:
- source_urls[0] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_busiest_airports_by_passenger_traffic): universe + ranking + value (Passengers 2025). Master article maintains an annual '2025 statistics' section; the article states 'For consistency, the Airports Council International's (ACI) annual figures are always used.' The article does NOT maintain an operational vs under-construction split — all ranked entries are operational. Master article ranks ~50 airports per ACI; staged 20 are the top-20 subset by 2025 passenger traffic.

decision_log:
Candidate card (Stage 1 pre-gate, then Stage 2 scored axes per instance_selection_priorities.md 4-axis rubric):
- Pre-gate verdict: PASS with five documented risks resolved at staging. R1: master 2025 statistics section is the most-recent year and is the canonical source — committed to 2025 snapshot at Stage-1 (mirrors ports 2024 snapshot pattern). R2: time-series Passengers metric — committed to master-wins canonical-source rule at Stage-1 (same as cycle-1 ports; the bridges/dams per-entity-wins rule applies to static structural metrics only). R3: Istanbul Airport Region ambiguity (Turkey straddles Europe + Middle East; airport on European side of Bosphorus) — committed to Region = Europe per master-article grouping at Stage-1, with Middle East alternative documented as open_question. R4: 3 master-vs-per-article name differences (Haneda, O'Hare, Dallas/Fort Worth) — committed to per-airport-article-title naming convention at Stage-1 (preserves Wikipedia common-form names with diacritics). Singapore Changi concurs (both master and per-article use 'Singapore Changi Airport'). R5: 6 per-airport articles with stale body-text passenger figures (Hartsfield–Jackson 108.1M-2024-body; Guangzhou 63.1M-2023-body; Shenzhen Bao'an 52.7M-2023-body; LA 76.59M-2024-body; Kuala Lumpur 57.08M-2024-body; DFW 81.76M-2023-body) — all resolved via master-wins rule.
- Seed/provenance: ORIGINAL. No example_questions.txt seed addresses airports. Closest seed-in-shape is the longest-rivers (top-K by physical dimension) and the just-staged container ports — airports are a same-shape entity class in a different Transportation/Aviation subdomain.
- Category: top_k (primary — single-cell-per-row attribute lookup over a fixed top-20-by-passenger-traffic entity set). Secondary: null (no clean second category; flat top-K, not partitioned). Saturates top_k at 5/5 — the 6th category to fully clear.
- Source plan: 21 Wikipedia URLs (1 master + 20 per-airport). Master defines universe + ranking + Passengers; per-airport articles supply Country + City.
- Expected shape: 20 rows × 5 cols, single PK on Airport.
- Domain: Transportation/Aviation — NEW subdomain (Transportation family at 2 instances becomes 3 with Aviation NEW). Domain novelty: Good (Transportation is the second-most under-represented family after the ports Logistics-NEW staging; with this Aviation NEW, Transportation becomes a 3-subdomain family).
- Entity-class diversity: `engineered-structures/airports` NEW fine-class. Bucket `engineered-structures/*` extends from 3 to 4 instances (joining bridges + buildings + dams + airports). Entity-class novelty: Good (NEW fine-class in mid-rep bucket).
- 4-axis rubric scoring: Seed source Bad (Original) + Category gap Good (gap-1 saturates 6th category) + Domain novelty Good (Aviation NEW subdomain in under-rep Transportation family) + Entity novelty Good (NEW fine-class) = ★★★ overall.
- Risks/adaptation: per the five pre-gate risks above. Additional minor risks: (a) row count 20 is at the upper end of standard 15-25 band; (b) US dominates the top-20 ranking (5 of 20 = 25%) — different distribution from ports (which had China 45%); (c) temporal_sensitivity = high reflects annual passenger shifts; (d) Region is curator-assigned (not directly source-grounded from per-airport articles); the 9-value closed vocabulary inherits from ports decision_log Rule 8 to maintain consistency between the two time-series-throughput top-K instances.
- Decision: STAGE.

Further decisions:
1) Universe rule: top-20 airports by 2025 annual passenger traffic per Wikipedia 'List of busiest airports by passenger traffic' master article's '2025 statistics' section (ACI sourced). All 20 are operational as of source-access date 2026-05-14. The master article enumerates ~50 airports; staged 20 are the top-20 subset.
2) **Canonical-source rule for time-series Passengers metric** (Stage-1 commitment, same as ports — applies the time-series-master-wins inversion of bridges/dams per-entity-wins): master wins for Passengers value because ACI is fresher than per-airport infoboxes which can lag by 2+ years. For non-time-series attributes (Country, City), per-airport article wins (entity-detail role). For Region (curator-assigned categorical), 9-value closed vocab per ports decision_log Rule 8. The same rule will apply to any future time-series-throughput top-K instance (e.g., busiest train stations, busiest seaports for tonnage, etc.).
3) Istanbul Airport Region = Europe: staged per master-article grouping. Turkey is a transcontinental country (Anatolia in Asia, European Turkey in Europe); Istanbul Airport is located on the European side of the Bosphorus (Arnavutköy district). Master article groups Istanbul under European rankings. Documented as open_question for the Middle East alternative reading.
4) Airport name normalization: Wikipedia common-form names per per-airport article title. 3 master-vs-per-article differences resolved in favor of per-airport article title (consistent with ports precedent): 'Haneda Airport' (master 'Tokyo Haneda Airport'); 'O'Hare International Airport' (master 'Chicago O'Hare International Airport'); 'Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport' (with slash per article URL; master 'Dallas Fort Worth' space-separated). 'Singapore Changi Airport' is a concurrence (both master and per-article use the same form — listed here only to flag the concurrence explicitly for audit). Diacritic preservation: 'Hartsfield–Jackson' uses en-dash (U+2013); 'Adolfo Suárez Madrid–Barajas' uses acute á (U+00E1) + en-dash; 'Shenzhen Bao'an' uses ASCII apostrophe (U+0027).
5) Country values: 13 distinct countries (United States 5, China 4, plus 11 singletons for UAE, Japan, UK, Turkey, India, South Korea, France, Singapore, Netherlands, Spain, Malaysia). Full-form country names per Wikipedia convention: 'United States' (not 'USA'); 'United Arab Emirates' (not 'UAE'); 'United Kingdom' (not 'UK'); 'South Korea' (not 'Republic of Korea').
6) City values: 20 distinct cities (one per airport; Singapore appears as both Country and City as a city-state). Conglomerate-city handling: Dallas/Fort Worth dual-city (per airport name + per article); Haarlemmermeer for Schiphol (per infobox precise municipality, mirrors Tanjung Pelepas → Iskandar Puteri precedent); Sepang for Kuala Lumpur (per infobox; airport is ~50 km from Kuala Lumpur). 'Tokyo' staged for Haneda as primary city (per-airport infobox cites Ōta ward of Tokyo; canonical primary city = Tokyo).
7) Passengers values: numeric millions per master article 2025 column (ACI sourced). Decimal precision: 1 (e.g., 106.3, 95.2, 91.7). All 20 staged Passengers values follow master per the time-series canonical-source rule (Decision 2). Some staged values disagree with per-airport infobox/body values which are stale by 1-2 years; documented in source_coverage_notes.
8) Region values: 9-value closed-vocab inherited from ports (East Asia / Southeast Asia / South Asia / Middle East / Europe / North America / Latin America / Africa / Oceania); 6 of 9 used in staged data (Latin America, Africa, Oceania declared but unused — only South Asia of the 'used' categories appears with 1 row). Region assignment follows the country-to-region mapping from ports decision_log Rule 8, with Istanbul → Europe per master-article grouping. Hong-Kong-style sub-national considerations do not apply (no Hong Kong airport in top-20).
9) Sort order: Passengers (millions) DESC primary (busiest-first), Airport ASC alphabetical secondary tiebreaker. No exact ties in staged 20 (the closest gap is 84.5 Heathrow vs 84.4 Istanbul, a 0.1 M gap — not a tie).
10) operation_type 'filter' chosen — top-K-by-Passengers is a filter operation (filter by 2025-Passengers rank ≤ 20). 'aggregation' was considered (GROUP BY region) but rejected because the universe is the top-20 directly, not a per-region aggregate.
11) claim_type 'source_defined' — universe is master-article-defined top-20 by 2025 passenger traffic. NOT `exhaustive` because the master article enumerates ~50 airports (only top-20 staged). NOT `partially_supplemented` because every row + every attribute is fully grounded across master (Passengers) + per-airport (Country, City) + curator-assigned (Region) sources.

open_questions: 1) **Time-series snapshot 2025**: master article's most-recent section is '2025 statistics' (ACI sourced; the 2025 column is full-calendar-year 2025 for 19 of 20 staged rows but Indira Gandhi's 2025 figure is Indian fiscal year April-2024 to March-2025 — see item 4 below for that exception). An LLM evaluator may have parametric knowledge from earlier years (2019-2024) producing different values — the 2020-2022 pandemic years caused major rank shifts (Chinese airports temporarily exceeded U.S. peaks, then receded). temporal_sensitivity = high acknowledges this; future-cycle refresh may update to 2026 column when ACI publishes. 2) **Canonical-source rule inversion** for time-series Passengers metric: this instance applies the same master-wins inversion established by the cycle-1 ports instance because ACI is fresher than per-airport infoboxes. Future audit could verify the inversion holds across all 20 rows. 3) **Istanbul Airport Region = Europe**: staged per master-article grouping (Istanbul Airport is located on the European side of the Bosphorus in Arnavutköy district). An LLM responding 'Middle East' is responding to the country-level framing (Turkey is geographically transcontinental) rather than the airport-location-level framing. Both readings defensible; staged follows master. 4) **Indira Gandhi 2025 figure represents Indian fiscal year April-2024 to March-2025**: master treats it as the 2025 row but the underlying period is fiscal-year not calendar-year. An LLM responding with a strict calendar-2025 reading might give a different value. Staged 79.3 M follows master. 5) **Schiphol City = Haarlemmermeer** (per infobox precise municipality) rather than 'Amsterdam' (canonical association): staged 'Haarlemmermeer' mirrors the ports Tanjung Pelepas → Iskandar Puteri precedent (per-entity infobox wins for precise municipality). An LLM responding 'Amsterdam' is responding to the canonical-association convention. Staged follows per-airport infobox. 6) **Kuala Lumpur Airport City = Sepang** (per infobox; airport is ~50 km from KL proper): same as Schiphol — staged precise municipality per infobox; alternative 'Kuala Lumpur' would be the canonical association. 7) **Haneda City = Tokyo** (primary city; infobox cites Ōta ward sub-component): An LLM responding 'Ōta' would be responding to the precise ward; staged 'Tokyo' follows canonical primary-city framing (different from Schiphol/KL because Ōta is a sub-ward of Tokyo, not an independent municipality, while Haarlemmermeer + Sepang ARE independent municipalities). 8) **Dallas/Fort Worth City = 'Dallas/Fort Worth'** (dual-city with slash per per-airport article): An LLM responding 'Dallas' alone would be reasonable but loses the dual-city information; 'Dallas–Fort Worth' with en-dash matches master rendering. Staged 'Dallas/Fort Worth' follows per-airport article URL/title. 9) **Master-vs-per-article name differences** (3 cases — Haneda, O'Hare, Dallas/Fort Worth; Singapore Changi concurs and is not a difference): staged per-airport-article-title form (Haneda Airport not Tokyo Haneda Airport; O'Hare International not Chicago O'Hare International; Dallas/Fort Worth not Dallas Fort Worth) mirrors the ports non-'Port of X' precedent. An LLM responding with master's longer form would match master but not per-article. 10) **Airport rank-21 boundary (Frankfurt, 63.2 M) within 0.1 M of rank-20 (KUL, 63.3 M)**: the staged top-20 cutoff is robust against single-row rounding but could shift in a 2026 update if Frankfurt or KUL passes the other. Universe rule remains 'top-20 per master' regardless of which airport occupies the boundary.
proposed_supplements:
The 20-row staged universe is a curator-bounded subset of the world's airports per Wikipedia master article 2025 column. Three curator-decided scope choices are documented:

(1) Top-K cutoff choice (20 vs 15 vs 25): the staged top-20 captures all airports with 63.3M+ 2025 passenger traffic. Alternatives:
- Top-15 (15 rows): would lose Incheon (74.1M), LAX (73.7M), CDG (72.0M), Beijing Capital (70.7M), Changi (70.0M), Schiphol (68.8M), Madrid-Barajas (68.2M), Shenzhen Bao'an (66.5M), KUL (63.3M). Plausible but loses major hubs.
- Top-25 (25 rows): would add Frankfurt (63.2M, just below KUL), Hong Kong International, Las Vegas Harry Reid, Tokyo Narita, Bangkok Suvarnabhumi. Plausible but adds row-count complexity beyond standard 15-25 band sweet spot.
- Top-20 (staged): standard sweet spot; captures meaningful regional diversity (13 countries across 6 regions).

(2) Time-series snapshot choice (2025 vs other year): staged 2025 follows the master article's current section header (ACI sourced). Alternatives:
- 2024 column: would shift values modestly; preserves the same top-20 set with minor rank changes; master no longer foregrounds 2024 as primary.
- 2023 column: pre-2024-recovery values; less canonical now.
- Multi-year average: would smooth temporal noise but break single-cell-per-row schema.
2025 single-year snapshot chosen because: (a) master article foregrounds the most-recent year; (b) ACI has explicit annual reporting cadence; (c) temporal_sensitivity = high already acknowledges annual shifts; (d) matches ports 2024 precedent (use master-article-current-year).

(3) Region vocabulary choice: 9-value closed vocabulary inherited from ports decision_log Rule 8 (East Asia / Southeast Asia / South Asia / Middle East / Europe / North America / Latin America / Africa / Oceania); 6 used in staged data. Alternative regionizations explored but rejected for consistency with ports: 'Asia-Pacific' too coarse; UN geographic regions too granular for top-20-row universe. The 9-value staged vocabulary balances granularity with parsimony across the two time-series-throughput top-K instances (ports + airports).

This is a curator-bounded `source_defined` instance — universe is master-article-defined top-K by 2025 passenger traffic. An audit could request expansion (top-25, top-30) or vocabulary revision based on alternative balancing.
